topic_title: SN2 Failure in Williamson Ether Synthesis

notes_list.title: Check Electrophile Structure
notes_list.basic_overview: Williamson ether synthesis works best with unhindered primary electrophiles because it proceeds through SN2 substitution.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
If the electrophile is tertiary, strong base and heat can favor elimination. For secondary substrates, substitution and elimination may compete. Redesign the synthesis so the alkoxide attacks a primary alkyl electrophile whenever possible.

MECHANISM & STEPWISE EXPLANATION
The source describes the transformation as: Williamson ether synthesis works best with unhindered primary electrophiles because it proceeds through SN2 substitution. The mechanism should be read as activation of the stated substrate, formation of the key reactive intermediate, the bond-making/bond-breaking event described by the reaction, and the stated work-up/product-forming step.

1. Activate the stated substrate with the listed reagent/conditions.
2. Generate the key reactive intermediate or electrophile/nucleophile implied by the reaction.
3. Carry out the characteristic bond-forming, bond-breaking or rearrangement step.
4. Complete proton transfer/work-up and verify the characteristic product.
